 Election Day is Tuesday: Where to vote, required ID and what you need to know in South Carolina 
 By FOX Carolina News Staff Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 11:37 AM EST | Updated : 57 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google GREENVILLE, S.C. (FOX Carolina) - South Carolina voters head to the polls Tuesday, Nov. 3, for the 2026 general election to decide key federal, state and local races.
 Early voting has concluded, meaning all in-person voting on Tuesday must take place under Election Day guidelines. Here is your complete guide to polling hours, identification requirements, booth rules and tracking live results.
 🕰️ When are polls open?
 Polls open statewide at  7 a.m. and close at 7 p.m. 
 The 7 p.m. rule:  Anyone in line by 7 p.m. is legally permitted to cast a ballot. Do not leave the line if 7 p.m. arrives and you have not yet voted. 
 📍Where do I vote?
 You must vote at your assigned precinct.  Unlike the early voting period, you cannot vote at any center in your county on Election Day. 
 Precinct locations frequently shift between election cycles. Verify your exact polling location and review your precinct-specific sample ballot at  scvotes.gov  before heading out. 
 🪪 What photo ID do I need?
 State law requires one of the following valid photo IDs to vote:
 South Carolina driver’s license (standard or REAL ID) 
 South Carolina DMV identification card 
 South Carolina voter registration card with a photo 
 Federal military ID (active duty, retiree or VA card) 
 U.S. passport 
 South Carolina concealed weapons permit 
 If you forget or do not have a photo ID, you can cast a provisional ballot after signing an affidavit citing a reasonable impediment (such as a lack of transportation, disability or work schedule). 
 🗳️ Returning an absentee ballot?
 Completed absentee ballots must be received by your county voter registration and elections office by  7 p.m. Tuesday . 
 Do not take mail-in absentee ballots to a polling precinct on Election Day; they must be hand-delivered to your county election office. 
 ✅ Rules inside the voting booth
 No ballot selfies:  South Carolina law prohibits voters from photographing marked ballots or using cameras inside the voting booth. 
 No campaign apparel (200-foot rule):  State law strictly bans campaign materials, signs and political clothing (including hats, shirts, buttons or stickers displaying candidate names or slogans) within 200 feet of any polling place entrance. Poll workers will require voters to remove or cover partisan apparel before entering. 
 Cell phones:  Voters are permitted to bring notes or reference sample ballots on their phones, but phone calls, recordings and photography are strictly prohibited inside the booth. 
 🚗 Curbside voting and voter assistance
 Curbside voting:  Every precinct in South Carolina is required by law to offer curbside voting for individuals with disabilities or voters who cannot enter the polling place without assistance. Designated curbside parking spaces with call buttons or monitors are stationed outside each site. 
 Assistance in the booth:  Any voter who has a disability or cannot read may receive assistance inside the booth from anyone of their choice, except their employer, an agent of their employer or an officer of their union. 
 ⛰️ Voting in Western North Carolina?
 For viewers in FOX Carolina’s Western North Carolina coverage area:
 North Carolina polls are open from  6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.  (anyone in line by 7:30 p.m. will be allowed to vote). 
 A valid photo ID is required to cast a ballot in North Carolina. 
 Voters can verify their registration, find their precinct and check sample ballots via the N.C. State Board of Elections at  ncsbe.gov . 
 📞 Encountering issues at the polls?
 If you experience problems casting your ballot or have questions on Election Day, contact:
 S.C. State Election Commission:  (803) 734-9060 
 Nonpartisan Election Protection Hotline:  1-866-OUR-VOTE (1-866-687-8683) 
 🔴 How to follow live results
 Polls close at 7 p.m., and results will begin trickling in shortly after.
 Bookmark FOX Carolina elections results and download the free FOX Carolina News app to receive breaking alerts and track live, real-time results for Upstate, Western North Carolina and statewide races throughout Tuesday night.
